subtitle: AI in the Spring ecosystem: ChatClient, advisors, embeddings, vector stores, and tool calling wired into Java services — enterprise patterns for storefront intelligence
audience: Java/Spring Boot developers (comfortable with controllers, beans, and configuration) who finished Prompt Engineering 101 and RAG Agents for E-commerce conceptually and now ship the same capabilities as production Java services. Version basis stated once, used everywhere: Spring AI 1.1+/2.x (verified against 2.0.1 reference), Spring Boot 3.x, Java 17+. Java runs in your Spring project; logic twins run as executable JS in the playground.
outcomes: Map the Spring AI landscape (ChatClient, advisors, RAG, tools, eval) and choose starters per need
Build ChatClient flows: builder beans, prompts, templates, defaults, entity outputs, streaming
Wire advisors: chat memory (with CONVERSATION_ID discipline), RAG question-answering, logging, ordering
Return structured entities with validation switches and provider-native output where supported
Expose POJO tools with @Tool methods and operate the ToolCallingAdvisor (auto-registration, ordering, user control)
Assemble RAG: ETL pipeline, pgvector store, QuestionAnswerAdvisor with metadata discipline
Evaluate with gold sets and observe via Micrometer observations + logger advisors
Ship a storefront assistant service: controller, RAG advisor, tools, eval gates, measured

assessment.q: Where does ChatClient.Builder come from in a Boot app, and why not ChatClient.create(model) directly?
options: Autoconfigured prototype Builder bean carries observability + customizers; create() bypasses them (use BuilderConfigurer path for multi-model instead)
assessment.explain: Auto-configured builders wire observability and customizers. Direct create() skips them — fine for scripts, wrong for services (Ch.2).

assessment.q: Memory advisor throws IllegalArgumentException at runtime. Most likely cause?
options: Missing ChatMemory.CONVERSATION_ID param on the call — required every time a memory advisor runs
assessment.explain: The ID param is mandatory per call with memory advisors. Absence fails fast at runtime, not compile time (Ch.3).

assessment.q: Advisor order: memory before RAG advisor. Why?
options: History must enter the prompt before retrieval runs, so search sees conversational context (follow-ups resolve pronouns correctly)
assessment.explain: Advisor chains execute in order with changes passed along: memory first enriches, RAG searches enriched. Order is semantics (Ch.3).

assessment.q: entity() returns garbage shaped correctly. Fix switches?
options: validateSchema() (retry with error feedback) + useProviderStructuredOutput() (API-level constraint) — validation and native constraints, composable
assessment.explain: EntityParamSpec switches: validate-then-retry plus provider-native schema enforcement. Shape-right-but-wrong needs validation loops (Ch.4).

assessment.q: Tools fire but never execute (definitions sent, calls ignored). Cause + fix?
options: ToolCallingAdvisor auto-registration disabled (property or per-call flag) — re-enable or drive user-controlled execution explicitly
assessment.explain: Definitions without execution = disabled auto-registration. Either re-enable or own the loop explicitly (Ch.5).

assessment.q: ToolCallingAdvisor must run inside a custom advisor's loop. Mechanism?
options: advisor-order property below the custom advisor's order (inside-loop) vs above (outside) — ordering positions repetition
assessment.explain: Order values place advisors inside/outside the tool loop. Default HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE+300; tune per placement need (Ch.5).

assessment.q: RAG answers ignore conversation follow-ups ('what about in blue?'). Fix?
options: Memory advisor BEFORE QuestionAnswerAdvisor so retrieval sees history-enriched queries
assessment.explain: Follow-ups need conversational context at retrieval time. Advisor order carries history into search (Ch.3/6).

assessment.q: Streaming endpoint needs entities (not yet supported reactively). Pattern?
options: Stream content, aggregate, then convert explicitly with a StructuredOutputConverter (BeanOutputConverter) — documented workaround
assessment.explain: Stream strings, collect, convert: the reference-documented bridge until reactive entities land. Workarounds stated as such (Ch.2).

assessment.q: StTemplateRenderer vs JSON in prompts conflict. Fix?
options: Custom delimiters (e.g. <>) via StTemplateRenderer builder — default {} collides with JSON braces
assessment.explain: Delimiter collision is mechanical: reconfigure start/end tokens. NoOpRenderer when no templating is wanted at all (Ch.2).

assessment.q: Logs show prompts but responses missing. Configuration?
options: SimpleLoggerAdvisor request/response mapping defaults: customize via constructor functions (request/response toString + order) — plus DEBUG level on the advisor package
assessment.explain: Advisor logging is configurable per direction with explicit order; package log level gates output. Configure, don't assume (Ch.7).

project.title: The Storefront Assistant Service
project.summary: Ship a Spring Boot service exposing a store assistant: ChatClient with memory + RAG advisors, catalog/order tools with a gated refund path, structured entities for decisions, streaming chat endpoint, gold-gated evaluation, and Micrometer observations — the Java production shape of everything this track taught in JS and Python.
requirements: ChatClient beans (default system + tools + advisors) with multi-model config where justified, observability retained
RAG: ETL-ingested catalog, pgvector store, QuestionAnswerAdvisor after memory advisor, metadata discipline
Tools: POJO @Tool methods (lookup, gated refund) with ToolCallingAdvisor ordering documented
Entities: decision/draft records via entity() with validateSchema on money paths
Streaming SSE endpoint plus sync JSON endpoint; documented entity-streaming workaround
Evaluation: gold conversation set with per-component attribution; no-regression gate on merges
Observability: SimpleLoggerAdvisor (DEBUG) + Micrometer observations with trace IDs in logs
technical: Version basis pinned (Spring AI 1.1+/2.x verified vs 2.0.1, Boot 3.x, Java 17+); deviations documented
Harness logic twins in runnable JS where behavior is engine-agnostic (routing, budgets, gates)
Secrets via environment only; no keys in code, logs scrubbed of PII
Numbers reproducible: gold sets, budgets, and eval scores committed
project.architecture: Five sections: (1) Service map — controllers, beans, advisors, tools, stores with versions; (2) Runs — traced conversations (happy/edge/gated) with per-component attribution; (3) Evaluation — gold scores, per-segment diffs, iterated fix; (4) Operations — observations, budgets, runbooks; (5) Honesty appendix — workarounds used (streaming entities, delimiter choices) with upstream links.
steps: Scaffold Boot service with ChatClient bean + /ai/health endpoint; verify via curl
Add memory + RAG advisors with CONVERSATION_ID discipline; prove follow-ups resolve
Add POJO tools with gated refund path; test invalid args and approval flow
Add entity outputs with validation switches; streaming endpoint with converter bridge
Build gold eval; baseline; iterate once on weakest segment; re-score
Instrument observations + logger advisor; write runbooks; assemble the evidence bundle
evaluation: Gated refund path demonstrated end to end with audit entries
Gold baseline + iteration with per-segment diffs on the same set
Observability shows traces with token/latency attributes; PII absent from logs
Workarounds documented with upstream references, not hidden
stretch: Add a second ChatModel (cost/quality routing) via BuilderConfigurer with @Primary documented
Dockerize with Testcontainers-based integration tests for RAG + tools
Expose an MCP server (Spring AI MCP boot starter) for the catalog tools

interviewQs.q: ChatClient.Builder bean vs ChatClient.create(model) — when each?
interviewQs.a: Autoconfigured Builder (prototype-scoped) for services: carries observability, customizers, and defaults; multi-model via BuilderConfigurer + @Primary to retain all wiring. create() for scripts/tests where observability doesn't matter. Bypass costs: direct builders skip customizers silently — the kind of gap found in production, not review.

interviewQs.q: Advisor ordering: memory before RAG — why does order matter?
interviewQs.a: Advisors execute in chain order passing modifications along: memory first injects history, then RAG searches with enriched queries (follow-ups resolve). Reversed, retrieval runs on bare follow-ups ('what about blue?' searches blue, not shoes). Order is semantics: each advisor transforms shared prompt state for the next.

Auto-registered unless disabled globally (spring.ai.chat.client.tool-calling.enabled=false), per call (AdvisorParams flag), or suppressed by providing your own ToolAdvisor. Order via advisor-order property (inside vs outside the loop). Own the loop explicitly (user-controlled execution) when streaming intermediates to UIs or customizing management.

interviewQs.q: entity() with validation — explain the switches.
interviewQs.a: EntityParamSpec.validateSchema() validates JSON against the entity schema with automatic retry-with-error-feedback; useProviderStructuredOutput() sends the schema as an API-level constraint where providers support it. Compose both for money paths. Converters (BeanOutputConverter) bridge streaming (aggregate-then-convert) until reactive entities land.

interviewQs.q: StTemplateRenderer delimiters vs JSON — resolve the conflict.
interviewQs.a: Default {} template syntax collides with JSON braces in prompts. Reconfigure delimiters (StTemplateRenderer.builder().startDelimiterToken('<')...) or use NoOpTemplateRenderer when no templating is wanted. Scoped per ChatClient via .templateRenderer() — advisor-internal templates have their own customization paths.

interviewQs.q: RAG in Spring AI: pieces and their order?
interviewQs.a: ETL pipeline (read/transform/write documents) → vector store (pgvector) → QuestionAnswerAdvisor in the ChatClient chain (after memory advisor) → entity/contract outputs. Metadata discipline (sku/version/date) carries over from RAG courses; SimpleLoggerAdvisor + Micrometer observations instrument; Testcontainers verify integration. Order: memory enriches, RAG retrieves, tools act, entities structure.
